scope: 112 original real-world documents, with all 27 historical failures separately reported; no duplicates
selection: User selected these three first; remaining five converters deferred, not reported as measured
execution: Sequential documents, persistent workers, rotating engine order; no builds or heavy checks during timings
timing: Reads, parse and Markdown export included; imports, result verification and transport excluded; in-conversion child process launch included
cpu: Per-conversion user+system CPU seconds via getrusage SELF plus waited-for CHILDREN; live/unreaped subprocess CPU is not captured; timeouts have missing CPU, never zero
memory: OS worker-lifetime RSS from /usr/bin/time -l including setup, warmup, parsing and transport; not an aggregate process-tree peak
failures: Keep every failed input. Report the full cohort and identical nonempty-returned subset. Returning output does not establish completeness. Partial recovery is a separate BulkParse profile, never substituted for defaults.
quality: No new LLM judging or paid jobs; retain outputs for source-scoped inspection. No quality score inferred from success, size or timing.
limits: Original BulkParse defaults, 90-second document deadline; no OCR or model downloads for this Office/EPUB corpus
source_freeze: Parser source, adapter source, installed versions, input/binary hashes and effective options recorded before conversion
